statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). NQ trades near 29,456.50, flat since the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, inside a 63.5-point band from 29,426.75 to 29,490.25, with two independent quote sources in agreement. Tokyo's cash open dipped to 63,067 on the Nikkei before recovering to 63,414, down 0.12%. Monday's Nasdaq-100 cash session closed at 29,127.16, down 0.82%, after a 1.63% gap-down open at 28,890.93 and a 417-point recovery from the 28,867.67 low. Tail sits at 16 in the low band because every observed leg so far has retraced. Stress is high at 66: WTI has extended about 1.2% overnight to roughly $102.6 with the Saudi East-West pipeline shut, the 10-year yield is 4.961% after rejecting a 5.012% print, the 30-year reached 5.38%, and futures markets price a high probability of a Federal Reserve rate increase on 16 September.
recommendation: Tail at 16 is in the low band, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. Four independent mean-reversion events are on the record: Monday's cash index recovered 417 points off its low, the 10-year yield's move above 5% was erased as buyers emerged, crude gave back part of a 5% intraday spike, and Tokyo's lower open this morning was bought back within the first quarter-hour. That is the opposite of a price path that denies retracement. The danger window is retained at 13:00 to 15:00 UTC on 15 September, covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour, where a second consecutive gap open after a chip-led de-rating is the specific structure that would matter. Conditional Tail peaks at 24 there, the top of the watch band, without reaching the block threshold. Stress stays high because a rates, energy and policy backdrop of this kind can still produce a large but recoverable drawdown.
headline: NQ holds a 63-point Globex band near 29,456.50 and Tokyo buys back a lower open, while crude extends 1.2% overnight toward $103 and the 10-year sits at 4.96% after Monday's 5% breach was rejected; Tail stays low at 16 with Stress high at 66 two days before a Federal Reserve decision priced for a rate increase
body:
The current hour rests on live evidence rather than an evidence gap. CME equity index futures reopened at 22:00 UTC and NQ has held a band 63.5 points wide, from 29,426.75 to 29,490.25, trading near 29,456.50 and up 0.02%. Two independent quote sources agree on the level. In Tokyo the Nikkei opened lower, traded down to 63,067 against a 63,492.99 previous close, and recovered to 63,413.85, a loss of only 0.12% within the first minutes of the cash session. An orderly reopen and a bought-back regional open are the most direct evidence available against a pathological price path.

Monday resolved as a two-sided, rotational session. The Nasdaq-100 cash index gapped 1.63% below the 29,368.44 previous close to open at 28,890.93, bottomed at 28,867.67, rallied 417 points to 29,285.50 and closed at 29,127.16, down 0.82%. The S&P 500 fell 0.48% and the Dow 0.29%. The decline was concentrated rather than index-wide: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell close to 6% as memory and equipment names were sold, while communication services rose. The trigger was a weekend essay from Anthropic's chief executive calling for the pace of frontier AI development to be slowed, followed by OpenAI confirming it will not seek a 2026 listing, which took SoftBank down 11% in Tokyo. Both the decline and the recovery retraced inside the day's range, which is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that defines tail risk.

The macro backdrop is where the stress sits. The 10-year Treasury yield briefly reached 5.012%, its first move above 5% since October 2023, before closing near 4.961%; the 30-year touched 5.38%, the highest since 2007. The driver is energy: Brent traded above $109 intraday, WTI is near $102.6 after extending roughly 1.2% overnight, the national average diesel price set an all-time high of $6.23 a gallon, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline remains shut after drone damage and may stay out of service for weeks, and an Iran-Gulf meeting on shipping safety was postponed. Futures markets now price a high probability that the Federal Reserve raises rates on 16 September, an unusually consequential meeting that also carries updated projections and a press conference.

That combination justifies high Stress and low Tail at the same time. The probability of a large but recoverable drawdown is elevated; the probability of a price path that denies retracement for long enough to overwhelm a mean-reverting approach is not, because the tape has retraced every leg it has produced in the last 24 hours. Shared cross-asset context collected at 22:47 UTC was 99 minutes old and partial at assessment time, so it was treated as stale and used only as weak confirmation of a quiet reopen; the assessment rests on independently verified live quotes and primary reporting.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments are available. Tail opened the window at 20, held a 19 to 21 plateau through the Asian session, rose to a 26 peak during the European morning chip-led decline, eased, repeated 26 at the US cash open, then decayed steadily through the afternoon to 15 by the Globex reopen as the opening gap was recovered. Stress fell from a 79 peak to 65 and Confidence held between 82 and 89. The window contains three hours in the orange band, all concentrated in the chip-led decline, and no hour reached the red band.
outlookSummary: The conditional path holds the low band through the remainder of the Asian session, with a small uplift at the Hong Kong and mainland opens, then eases to an overnight floor of 16. It rises to 18 for the European opening auction and 19 at the London open, enters the watch band at 20 across the European mid-morning that produced Monday's chip-led leg, steps to 21 for the 12:15 and 12:30 UTC releases, and peaks at 24 across the 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour. It eases to 21 in the midday lull, returns to 22 for the 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC, holds at 21 into the final cash hour before Federal Reserve decision day, then falls to 19 after the cash close, 17 during the CME maintenance halt and 18 at the Globex reopen. No hour in the window reaches the block threshold on current evidence. Stress stays in the high band throughout, peaking at 74 in the first full cash hour, and Confidence decays from 88 to 76 with forecast distance.
